title: Training refits widened ozone and warmth score ranges under cluster weights in four US bird transfers in 1995-2024
abstract: We tested how training uncertainty changes a published ozone and warmth prediction result. We used 23,357 annual US bird survey pairs and kept four published time transfers. We compared fixed models with models fitted again under 4,999 positive state or year cluster weights. Training refits widened the 98.75 percent score ranges by factors of 1.98 to 7.64. All eight refit ranges included zero. Thus, the prior lack of a clear gain from the ozone and warmth product remained. These are sensitivity ranges with unknown confidence coverage. The records are reused, and no independent biological validation is claimed. Few clusters, changing monitors, detection bias and untested space-time dependence limit use. Code, input hashes, paired draw results and numerical checks are included.

display.caption: Refit and fixed-model 98.75 percent score ranges under identical state or year weights. Negative scores favor the ozone and warmth product. These are sensitivity ranges with unknown confidence coverage.
